verdict.rationale: Carta's API uses OAuth 2.0 applications with a client-credentials grant and configurable OAuth scopes, plus service-account-style apps bound to an investment firm. Together these are a first-party way to issue scoped machine credentials that an agent could use. However, the evidence only says scopes can be added to extend capabilities; it does not show fine-grained least-privilege controls or agent-specific credential handling. Missing for 10: documented scope granularity (e.g., read-only vs. write per resource), explicit least-privilege guidance, agent-specific credential issuance or revocation/rotation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Carta's API uses the OAuth 2.0 open specification to authorize your access to our data, and supports AUTHORIZATION_CODE and CLIENT_CREDENTIALS grant types.
Adding new OAuth scopes to your OAuth application allows you to enhance the capabilities of your integration with the Carta API platform.
The client credentials flow provides access to data about your company and does not require explicit permission from a Carta user prior to accessing that data.
The application is now added to your Investment Firm and can be used to access its data via the Investor API
